questions.question: Let $N$ be a Poisson process with rate $\lambda>0$, where $N(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$ and $A_k$ is the time of the $k$th arrival. Fix $t>0$ and $n\ge1$. Conditional on $N(t)=n$, the vector $(A_1,\dots,A_n)$ has the same distribution as which random vector?
options: $n$ i.i.d. $\operatorname{Unif}([0,t])$ variables, kept in the order in which they were drawn
$n$ i.i.d. $\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$ variables, sorted from smallest to largest
The order statistic $(U_{(1)},\dots,U_{(n)})$ of $n$ i.i.d. $\operatorname{Unif}([0,t])$ variables
The fixed vector $\big(t/(n+1),\,2t/(n+1),\,\dots,\,nt/(n+1)\big)$ of equally spaced times

questions.question: Let $N$ be a Poisson process with rate $\lambda>0$, where $N(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$ and $A_k$ is the time of the $k$th arrival. Fix $t>0$ and $n\ge1$. How does the conditional joint law of $(A_1,\dots,A_n)$ given $N(t)=n$ depend on the rate $\lambda$?
options: It does not depend on $\lambda$: its density is $n!/t^n$ on $\{0<t_1<\dots<t_n<t\}$
A larger $\lambda$ shifts the conditional arrival times towards the start of $[0,t]$
It contains $\lambda$ through a factor $\lambda^n\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda t}$ in the joint density
It is free of $\lambda$ only when $\lambda t=n$, so that the count equals its mean

questions.question: Let $N$ be a Poisson process with rate $\lambda>0$, where $N(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$ and $A_k$ is the time of the $k$th arrival. The arrival-time recursion is $A_k=A_{k-1}+X_k$ with $A_0=0$ and i.i.d. $X_k\sim\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$. With no conditioning on any count, what is the distribution of the first arrival time $A_1$?
options: $\operatorname{Unif}([0,t])$ for any fixed $t>0$, because Poisson arrivals are uniform
$\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$ with mean $1/\lambda$, since $A_1=X_1$
$\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)$, since the arrivals come from a Poisson process
$\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$ restricted to $[0,t]$, since arrivals lie in $[0,t]$

questions.question: Let $N$ be a Poisson process with rate $\lambda>0$, where $N(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$ and $A_k$ is the time of the $k$th arrival. Given $N(t)=n$, the conditional joint density of $(A_1,\dots,A_n)$ equals the constant $n!/t^n$. On which set of points $(t_1,\dots,t_n)$ does this value apply, the density being $0$ elsewhere?
options: Every point of the cube $(0,t)^n$, ordered or not
The points with $0<t_1<\dots<t_n$, with no upper bound
The points with $(k-1)t/n<t_k<kt/n$ for each $k$
The ordered points with $0<t_1<t_2<\dots<t_n<t$

questions.question: Let $N$ be a Poisson process with rate $\lambda>0$, where $N(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$ and $A_k$ is the time of the $k$th arrival. Fix $t>0$ and $n\ge2$. Given $N(t)=n$, are the arrival times $A_1,\dots,A_n$ independent?
options: No: they are dependent, since $A_1<A_2<\dots<A_n$ always holds
Yes: given the count, each $A_k$ is an independent $\operatorname{Unif}([0,t])$
Yes: the Poisson process has independent increments, so they are independent
No: given the count the gaps $A_k-A_{k-1}$ are still i.i.d. $\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$, and sums of shared gaps are dependent

questions.question: Calls arrive as a Poisson process with rate $\lambda=6$ per hour; time is in minutes and $A_1$ is the first call time. Given that exactly one call came in the hour, $N(60)=1$, what is $\mathbb{P}(A_1\le20\mid N(60)=1)$?
options: $1-\mathrm{e}^{-2}\approx0.865$
$\mathrm{e}^{-2}\approx0.135$

questions.question: Jobs arrive as a Poisson process with rate $\lambda=3$ per hour, time in minutes, and $A_k$ is the $k$th arrival time. Given $N(60)=5$, what is the conditional mean $\mathbb{E}[A_2\mid N(60)=5]$?
options: $24$ minutes
$30$ minutes
$40$ minutes
$20$ minutes

questions.question: Customers arrive as a Poisson process $N$ with rate $\lambda=5$ per hour, time in minutes. Given that $N(120)=6$ customers arrived in two hours, what is $\mathbb{E}[N(30)\mid N(120)=6]$, the expected number in the first $30$ minutes?
Requests arrive as a Poisson process $N$, time in minutes. Given that $N(30)=3$, what is the probability that the first $10$ minutes contain no request, $\mathbb{P}(N(10)=0\mid N(30)=3)$?

To simulate a Poisson process on $[0,60]$ given $N(60)=4$, four i.i.d. $\operatorname{Unif}([0,60])$ values are drawn and come out as $41,\ 12,\ 55,\ 7$ in draw order. What is the simulated third arrival time $A_3$?

For a Poisson process with rate $\lambda$, $n=2$ and $0<t_1<t_2<t$, the probability that the first two arrivals fall in $[t_1,t_1+\mathrm{d}t]$ and $[t_2,t_2+\mathrm{d}t]$ and the third after $t$ is $\lambda\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda t_1}\mathrm{d}t\cdot\lambda\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda(t_2-t_1)}\mathrm{d}t\cdot\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda(t-t_2)}=\lambda^2\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda t}\,\mathrm{d}t^2$. What does this show?
options: Placements with a small $t_1$ are likelier, as $\lambda\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda t_1}$ decreases in $t_1$
Given $N(t)=2$, every ordered placement $0<t_1<t_2<t$ is equally likely
Given $N(t)=2$, the times $A_1$ and $A_2$ are independent $\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$
Given $N(t)=2$, the law of the placement still depends on $\lambda$ via $\lambda^2\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda t}$

questions.question: Let $N$ be a Poisson process with rate $\lambda>0$, where $N(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$ and $A_k$ is the time of the $k$th arrival. Fix $t>0$, $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$. Which statement about the conditional law of the single arrival time $A_k$ given $N(t)=n$ is correct?
options: $A_k\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,t])$ for each $k$, because the joint law is uniform on its region
$A_k\sim\operatorname{Unif}([(k-1)t/n,\,kt/n])$, the $k$th of $n$ equal slots of $[0,t]$
$A_k$ is the $k$th smallest of $n$ uniforms on $[0,t]$, so it has mean $kt/(n+1)$
$A_k$ is the $k$th of $n$ equally spaced times, so it has mean $kt/n$

questions.question: Let $N$ be a Poisson process with rate $\lambda>0$, where $N(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$ and $A_k$ is the time of the $k$th arrival. Fix $0<s<t$ and $n\ge1$. Which statement correctly compares the law of $N(s)$ with and without conditioning on $N(t)=n$?
options: Unconditionally $N(s)\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda s)$; given $N(t)=n$, $N(s)\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,s/t)$, free of $\lambda$
Both laws are $\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda s)$, as conditioning on a later count leaves $N(s)$ unchanged
Unconditionally $N(s)\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda s)$; given $N(t)=n$, $N(s)\sim\operatorname{Pois}(ns/t)$
Unconditionally $N(s)\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda s)$; given $N(t)=n$, $N(s)$ is uniform on $\{0,\dots,n\}$

questions.question: Let $N$ be a Poisson process with rate $\lambda>0$, where $N(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$ and $A_k$ is the time of the $k$th arrival. Given $N(10)=2$, the first arrival $A_1$ is the minimum of two i.i.d. $\operatorname{Unif}([0,10])$ points. What is the conditional density of $A_1$ at $s=2$?

Calls arrive as a Poisson process with rate $\lambda=5$ per hour, and arrival times on $[0,60]$ in minutes are to be simulated, the number $N(60)$ of calls being random. Which procedure produces correctly distributed arrival times $A_1<A_2<\dots<A_{N(60)}$?
options: Take $\lambda t=5\cdot60=300$, sample a $\operatorname{Pois}(300)$ count, and sort that many uniforms on $[0,60]$
Draw $n\sim\operatorname{Pois}(5)$, then draw $n$ uniforms on $[0,60]$ and sort them
Set $n=5$, the expected count, then draw five uniforms on $[0,60]$ and sort them
Draw $n\sim\operatorname{Pois}(5)$, then use $n$ uniforms on $[0,60]$ in draw order

questions.question: Let $N$ be a Poisson process with rate $\lambda>0$, where $N(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$ and $A_k$ is the time of the $k$th arrival. Given $N(10)=3$, what is the value of the conditional joint density of $(A_1,A_2,A_3)$ at the point $(t_1,t_2,t_3)=(2,5,9)$?

An arrival process has inter-arrival times exactly $12$ minutes each, so the gaps are i.i.d. but deterministic, and $N(60)$ counts arrivals in $[0,60]$, giving $N(60)=5$. Is $(A_1,\dots,A_5)$ given $N(60)=5$ distributed as five sorted $\operatorname{Unif}([0,60])$ variables?
options: Yes: the count $N(60)=5$ is known, and the count alone fixes the conditional law
Yes: the gaps are i.i.d., and i.i.d. gaps are all the result requires
No: the result needs the gaps themselves to be uniformly distributed, and constant gaps are not uniform
No: the times are fixed at $12,24,36,48,60$; the result needs exponential gaps

questions.question: Let $N$ be a Poisson process with rate $\lambda>0$, where $N(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$ and $A_k$ is the time of the $k$th arrival. Fix $t>0$ and condition on the event $\{N(t)\ge1\}$ instead of on an exact count. Is $A_1$ given $N(t)\ge1$ uniform on $[0,t]$?
options: No: for $0\le s\le t$ the conditional distribution function is $\frac{1-\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda s}}{1-\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda t}}$
Yes: conditioning on any event about the count $N(t)$ removes $\lambda$, so $A_1$ is uniform on $[0,t]$
Yes: the law mixes the laws of $A_1$ given $N(t)=n$ over $n\ge1$, and each of these is uniform on $[0,t]$
No: $A_1$ given $N(t)\ge1$ is still $\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$ on $[0,\infty)$, by the memoryless property

questions.question: Calls arrive as a Poisson process $N$, time in minutes, with $A_k$ the $k$th call time. Given $N(60)=5$, what is $\mathbb{P}(A_2\le20\mid N(60)=5)$?
